Sirén: his “adherence to the ‘spirit of the ancients’ (ku-i)”

bio.text: From my youth I loved to paint. Whenever I obtained a bit of silk or a piece of paper, I could not resist grasping the brush and making a drawing.
bio.lead: Zhao Mengfu, writing late in life:

source.author: Zhao Mengfu (Chao Meng-fu)
source.title: Colophon on one of his early paintings
source.publisher: translated in Osvald Sirén, A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II (The Medici Society, 1933; Internet Archive scan)

bio.text: The foremost official representative of painting and calligraphy in the reign of Kublai Khan and of his three successors was Chao Meng-fu, often called by his tzu, Tzu-ang, or by his hao, Sung-hsiieh Tao-jen (The Sage of the Pines and the Snow).

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II

bio.text: It may be said of Chao Meng-fu that his was a combination of literary, calligraphic, and artistic talent such as no other single man in the long history of China has ever [displayed].

source.author: John C. Ferguson
source.title: Chinese Painting
source.publisher: University of Chicago Press (Internet Archive scan)
